answer: New agent identities start weak and must climb a spiral of escalating proof-of-work: each capability tier needs a fresh, harder puzzle bound to the identity's public key, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousand times the compute. A beacon publishes unpredictable audit seeds each round, and randomly chosen peers re-verify a sample of recent work; a sparrow-light identity that cannot show its chain of solved puzzles is quarantined before it can trade. Attackers pay real, rising compute per fake identity and face constant exposure, while honest agents pay once and reuse proven work.
